# Keep app view state in the URL

Every workspace app (/app/<name>) keeps its view state (folder, open item, search, filter, workspace) in the URL, so refresh restores it and Back and Forward move between views. Mail (src/components/LiveMail.tsx) is the reference.

1. Declare the app's parameters once in `appViews` in `src/lib/app-view.ts` (each key with a check: uuid, id, text, day or oneOf) and give its route in `src/router.tsx` `validateSearch: appSearch('<app>')`; the router reads and writes plain string parameters (`parseSearch`, `stringifySearch`). Names: Mail `mailbox`, `folder`, `message`, `q`, `label`; Drive `folder` (an id or `trash`), `file`, `q`, `label`; Chat `room`, `q`; Calendar `view` (month, week, day or list), `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `calendar`, `event`, `instance`; Contacts and Loop `contact`, `q`; Meet `meeting`; every app `workspace`, which wins over the stored preference. Settings keep their paths.
2. Read and change the view with `const { view, set } = useAppView('<app>', { onInvalid })`. Derive what is open from `view`; never mirror it in useState. Defaults stay out of the URL (no `folder` means Inbox). Open another app at a view with `useOpenApp()(app, view)`, which keeps `?workspace=`.
3. Push or replace: `set(patch)` pushes a history entry for opening a folder, an item or an app; `set(patch, { replace: true })` for typing a search, changing a filter, and returning to the list after the open item left it. A key set to undefined leaves the URL. Bind a search box with `useViewText(view.q, write)` so typing answers from local state while the URL follows (replace); a new search returns to the result list (`message: undefined`). The top navigation (`src/components/LiveWorkspace.tsx`) remembers each app's last view in the tab, so leaving an app and coming back restores it; the current app's link goes to its start.
4. Actions: after one that removes the open item from the current list (archive, trash, restore, move to spam), patch the cached lists, return to the list in the URL with nothing selected (`set({ message: undefined }, { replace: true })`) and show a notice from `useNotice()` rendered with `<AppNotice notice={notice} clear={clear} />` (`src/components/AppNotice.tsx`; it clears itself after a timeout and when the user leaves the app's page), with Undo when the API can reverse it. In-place actions (star, read, screening review) update the cache from the response at once and confirm with a role=status notice; failures show role=alert with `userError`.
5. Fallbacks: the one component that owns the app passes `onInvalid`, which strips malformed values (replace) and shows a notice. A stale item id (a 4xx from its query; do not retry 4xx) or a foreign workspace drops the parameter with replace and shows a notice. Never a blank page or a crash.
6. Test it in `e2e/` like `e2e/navigation-state.spec.ts`, at 390px and 1440px: refresh keeps the folder and the open item, Back closes the item and then returns to the previous folder, actions return to the list with their notice, stale and invalid links fall back with a notice. Run `lidza check --json` and `lidza test --e2e`.
